lineas.texto: How does a tiny piece of metal open a locked door?
Inside the lock there's a cylinder, the plug. Turn it, and the door opens.
But five stacks of pins, pushed down by springs, block it from turning.
Put in the wrong key, and the pins stop at the wrong heights. Stuck.
The right key has cuts at exactly the right depths.
Each cut lifts its pin until the gap lands right on this line, the shear line.
Nothing crosses the line anymore, so the plug is free to turn.
The plug drags the bolt back into the door, and it swings open.
